meta.title: Russian Monument Sofia (Руски паметник) – History, Map & Visitor Guide
meta.description: Visiting the Russian Monument in Sofia? Discover the history of the 1877-1878 Russo-Turkish War landmark, location maps, tram routes, and 24/7 visitor info.

intro.title: About The Russian Monument in Sofia
intro.breadcrumb: The Russian Monument in Sofia › Sofia › Sofia City Province › Bulgaria
intro.description: Welcome to The Russian Monument in Sofia, widely recognized simply as the Russian Monument (Руски паметник). Located in the heart of Sofia, Bulgaria, this historic landmark commemorates the Russian soldiers who liberated Bulgaria from Ottoman rule in 1878 and stands as a symbol of Bulgarian-Russian friendship and gratitude.
intro.nearby: When visiting The Russian Monument in Sofia, visitors can easily explore surrounding historical landmarks and points of interest, including Alexander Nevsky Cathedral and St. Sofia Church.

visitGuide.title: Visit Tips
items: The monument is accessible 24/7 as it's an outdoor landmark.
Best time to visit is during daylight hours for photos.
Located in a busy intersection, be careful when crossing streets.
Combine your visit with nearby attractions like St. Sofia Church.

sections.title: History & Significance
sections.content: The Russian Monument was unveiled on 29 June 1882, the first monument built in Sofia after the Liberation. It honors the Russian soldiers who fell during the Russo-Turkish War (1877-1878), which ended nearly five centuries of Ottoman rule over Bulgaria. The project was funded by donations collected from the Russian people; the names of the designers remain unknown to official records.

sections.title: Architecture & Design
sections.content: The monument is a truncated four-sided pyramid (obelisk) set on a three-step base. On its western side it bears the inscription "Не нам, не нам, а имени Твоему" ("Not unto us, not unto us, but to Thy name") with the dates 1877-1878. The eastern side features a stone relief of the coat of arms of the Russian Empire together with a St George Cross, a Russian military decoration. All inscriptions on the monument are in Russian.

sections.title: Location & Surroundings
sections.content: The monument is situated at the intersection of Makedonia Boulevard and Evlogi Georgiev Boulevard in Sofia Center. The location, known in Bulgarian as пл. „Руски паметник" (Ploshtad "Ruski Pametnik", Russian Monument Square), is a major traffic junction and public space in the city.

sections.title: Preservation & Status
sections.content: The Russian Monument is protected as a cultural heritage site by the Bulgarian government. Over the years, it has undergone several restorations to preserve its historical and artistic value. It remains one of Sofia's most recognizable landmarks.

items.question: Where is The Russian Monument located?
items.answer: The monument is located at pl. "Ruski pametnik", blvd. "Makedonia" 51, 1606 Sofia, Bulgaria. The location is well-served by public transport.

items.question: Is there an entrance fee?
items.answer: No, the monument is an outdoor public landmark that can be viewed free of charge at any time.

items.question: What are the visiting hours?
items.answer: As an outdoor monument, it is accessible 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. However, daytime visits are recommended for the best experience and safety.

items.question: How do I get to the monument?
items.answer: The monument is accessible by public transport: trams 4, 5 and 15 stop at the "Руски паметник" stop at the square, and buses and trolleys stop nearby on Makedonia Boulevard. Metro Line 3 is about a 10-15 minute walk away. Taxis and ride-sharing services are also readily available in Sofia.

items.question: What landmarks are near the Russian Monument?
items.answer: The Russian Monument stands near several major Sofia landmarks, including Alexander Nevsky Cathedral, St. Sofia Church and the National Archaeological Museum – all within a 10–20 minute walk.

items.question: Is the Russian Monument accessible to visitors with reduced mobility?
items.answer: The monument is an outdoor landmark in an open public square and can be approached from the surrounding pavements. Some crossings may be uneven, so visitors with mobility needs are advised to approach from the main pavement along Makedonia Boulevard.

transport.title: How to Get Here
transport.fromCenterDesc: The monument sits in Sofia Center at the junction of Makedonia and Evlogi Georgiev boulevards, about a 15-20 minute walk from the central pedestrian zone and most major hotels.
transport.fromStationDesc: The "Руски паметник" (Ruski Pametnik) tram stop is served by tram lines 4, 5 and 15. Bus and trolley lines also stop on Makedonia Boulevard.
transport.fromAirportDesc: Take the metro (Line 1 or 2) to Serdika Station, then transfer to a tram, bus or trolley towards Ruski Pametnik, or continue by taxi.
transport.publicTransportDesc: Trams 4, 5 and 15 stop at the "Руски паметник" stop at the square; bus lines 72, 76, 204 and trolleys 5, 8 stop nearby on Makedonia Boulevard. Metro Line 3 is about a 10-15 minute walk away.
transport.walkingDesc: About 20-25 minutes from Alexander Nevsky Cathedral, or 15-20 minutes from the central pedestrian zone and Vitosha Boulevard.
transport.drivingDesc: Located on Makedonia Boulevard, a major thoroughfare in Sofia, at the junction with Evlogi Georgiev Boulevard.

items.name: Public Restrooms
items.description: Public toilets are limited directly around the busy junction. The nearest restrooms are typically inside nearby shopping centres, hotels and cafés, which generally welcome visitors; plan ahead before long walks.

items.name: Parking
items.description: Paid on-street parking (blue and green zones) operates in the surrounding streets, free on Sundays and outside charging hours. Spaces are limited and the area is busy, so public transport is recommended.
items.hint: Paid street parking · paid car parks nearby

items.name: Dining & Cafés
items.description: A wide choice of restaurants, cafés, bakeries and fast-food places sits within a short walk, including traditional Bulgarian taverns serving local cuisine. We list types only, not specific businesses.

items.name: Hotels & Accommodation
items.description: Sofia's city centre offers hotels, boutique hotels, apartments and hostels within walking distance of the monument, suitable for all budgets.

items.name: Shops & Supermarkets
items.description: Convenience stores and supermarkets are scattered across the centre, with larger shopping centres about 10-15 minutes away on foot.

items.name: Fuel & EV Charging
items.description: Petrol stations are scarce in the city centre, so refuel before entering Sofia. Public electric-vehicle charging points are available at some car parks and public areas.

items.distance: About 11 km · by car or bus
